articles.author: By null
articles.body: Contrary to rumors, classes will be held Labor Day, Monday, Sept. 5., according to James Pitts, dean of academic affairs. Only non-teaching staff members will have the day off.

articles.headline: Senior Registration
articles.author: By null
articles.body:
Registration has now started for seniors at the CAP Center, Susan Bartel, coordinator for the Career Advising and Placement Center, said this week.

By registering at the CAP Center, students can establish a credential file and stay aware of job opportunities. A credential file consists of a resume, recommendation sheet, and a data sheet, and it acts as a "holding file" for references that need to be sent to graduate schools and employers, Bartel said.

Once seniors register, they can participate in the recruiting program, which allows them to interview with companies that recruit at Ohio Wesleyan. Students are also notified of job opportunities outside of the recruiting program.

Seniors wanting to sign up are required to attend a registration workshop. A workshop is held each day at the CAP Center, according to Bartel.

The workshops will also be held in the living units and continue until the end of October.

articles.headline: Rush to promote entire Greek system
articles.author: By RACHEL RHODES Staff Reporter
articles.body:
The primary aim of rush this fall is to promote the entire Greek system, instead of focusing on individual fraternities and sororities, Nancy Bihl Rutkowski, coordinator of Greek affairs, said this week.

Jim Holland, IFC rush chairperson, said, "We want to promote the Greek system as one fraternity this year. It's more important to get the freshmen to go Greek, rather than to talk so much about the separate houses."

Men's rush will be Sept. 7-16, with its pledge day on Sept. 17. As a way to unify the Greek system, the IFC will hold a pledge education workshop on Sept. 20 for all male pledges to learn the history, services, rules and expectations of the IFC. The IFC is also holding a rush orientation workshop tonight at 7 p.m. in the MUB Ballroom. Holland and IFC President Lee Williams will explain rush procedures.

Women's rush will be Sept. 19-25, with its pledge day on Sept. 26. Ohio Wesleyan's new sorority, Delta Zeta, will hold its first rush party Sept. 19, but will continue the remaining days of its rush on Sept 27. Prior to rush, Panhel is holding rush information meetings for everyone signed up on Tuesday, Sept. 6, and Tuesday, Sept. 13. Both meetings will be at 7 p.m. in Stuy Smoker.

The rush kick-off will be Sunday, Sept. 18, at 2 p.m. Panhel Co-Rush Chairpersons Katie Hess and Anne Werner said they also want to unify and strengthen the Greek system. To increase faculty involvement in rush, they sent a letter to all faculty members last spring, and sent Greek representatives to speak at the academic open house this fall. They are also selling T-shirts in the MUB and sending letters to parents.

Rutkowski said she feels much more at ease with rush this year, partly because the party scheduling and bid matching will be computerized for the first time.

A judicial board has also been organized to handle any possible "dirty rushing." An active member making a rushee feel uncomfortable by pressuring him or her to join a certain house is an example of dirty rushing, Rutkowski said. The board will consist of one member from each sorority and fraternity and two alumni advisers. This year the advisers will be from Delta Tau Delta and Delta Gamma. The advisers will change each year alphabetically according to the names of the fraternities and sororities. Rutkowski added that infractions must be reported to the board within three days.

Anyone interested in signing up for rush can do so in Smith Lobby and the MUB.

articles.headline: Sports Focus
articles.author: By null
articles.body:
The Transcript will be covering lots of sports this year, but it's not because there is no news to cover or because we hold sports coverage high above other activities on campus.

The simple fact is that this year, more than any other year in the history of the university, sports will be a main topic on campus. Our coverage of sports should be expected even if just for this year's National Colloquium topic. But there are other reasons.

Ohio Wesleyan gained national fame last year when Gene Mehaffey's basketball team trounced Scranton University 92-70 for the Division III National Championship at Calvin College in Grand Rapids, Mich. The Transcript feels the need to keep up to date on this sport as well as the other teams that have a habit of gaining national recognition -- the men's soccer and lacrosse teams and the field hockey team.

In addition to the recent success of our sports teams, which includes an up-and-coming football program that two years ago was as good as dead, there is a sports and fitness small-living unit on campus.

News is sports, sports is news. But, the many sports-related news stories may make it appear that that's all we care about. We hope the sports stories will be interesting to all of our readers, whether they be sports fans or not.

articles.headline: Get involved in WCSA
articles.author: By Jim Foley
articles.body:
Dear Students,

Now is your chance to get involved with student government at Ohio Wesleyan!

The Wesleyan Council on Student Affairs (WCSA) wants ten outgoing and eager geographic representatives to participate on the body for the 1988-89 academic year.

Geographic representatives are responsible for distributing information to the residents of their geographic area (housing units) and find out what these residents would like to see WCSA work on. Representatives must also attend the regular WCSA meetings to voice their concerns and exercise their voting power on campus issues. The schedule for the Geographic Representative Elections will be as follows:

Friday, Sept. 9 -- Organizational Meeting MUB Ballroom 4 p.m.

Friday, Sept. 16 -- Registration Deadline MUB Desk 4 p.m.

Monday-Wednesday Sept. 19-21 -- Campaigning

Thursday-Friday Sept. 22-23 -- Voting

The breakdown for the Geographic Representative seats on the WCSA body are:

articles.headline: Men's soccer tries to meet expectations
articles.author: By TOM JAMES Staff Reporter
articles.body:
It was never said that a 19-4 season, or a 39-7 mark over two seasons, would be easy to repeat. Jay Martin and his Bishop soccer team are likely to find this truer than ever in the fall of '88, as they have lost three crucial starters to graduation and another to the injury bug, as they face a schedule that includes a pair of Division I opponents in the early going.

Gone are two-time All-America goalkeeper Jeff Kaplan, forward and set-up man Domenic Romanelli and 23-goal-scoring front-liner Charlie Blanchard, who will help Martin and coach the JV team this year.

The biggest, and possibly most devestating, shake-up is a severe knee injury to captain Peter Pak. The junior midfielder blew out the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during the preseason and is gone for the year.

The combined loss of Blanchard and Pak has resulted in a multi-player shift on the offense, which outscored its opposition 68-16 last season. The cushion for all of this is the return of senior Bob Burnes, who popped home 20 goals in the '87 campaign.

Barnes will be joined up front by sophomore Scott Gillanders and freshman Andy Kessenger. Junior Mike Ellis is the only returning forward on the bench.

Martin has deemed the midfield as pivotal to any continued team success. Starting, after the loss of Pak, will be junior Trip Roney, senior Eric Warn, and sophomores Matt Schrader and Dennis Peacock. Schrader is a newcomer to the varsity team. Senior Matt Miller will move up from the backfield, though he'll start on the bench along with sophomore Matt Williams.

The backbone of this outfit is the defense. Seniors Drew Dimatos, Clark Howell, and Leo Chappel are the starting back line for the third straight year. Dimatos had seven goals last season, the kind of production from the back that will be most appreciated by the otherwise-depleted Ohio Wesleyan attack.

"With Dimatos, any group is a good group," said Martin, about the high-scoring defender.

The unenviable task of "replacing" Kaplan falls on the shoulders of sophomore Ian Meyer and freshman Reed Welch. Meyer, who saw action just twice last year, will start for the time being, but, according to Martin, will split playing time with Welch. The lack of experience in the nets will, nonetheless, make the role of the veteran defenders just that much more important.

Along with the changes on offense, there are two Division I teams on the schedule in the first three weeks of the Bishops' 20-game regular-season schedule, though both games will be at home. The first is tonight's season-opener against Dayton, with a 7:30 kickoff. The other will be September 20 with Akron, which knocked off the Bishops last year at Akron, 2-1. Martin recognizes the importance of the September action, and the Division I foes, to the season.

"[Our schedule is] top-heavy. We'll know where we stand by Oct. 1," said Martin.

This week's other action, set for Friday and Saturday, will be the Bishop-hosted Frank Myers Tournament, named after the former Bishop soccer mentor.

However, this year's tourney is, in effect, not a tournament, because the second-round pairings have been preset. In Friday's action, North Carolina Wesleyan will play Otterbein at 5 p.m., before Ohio Wesleyan's 7:30 meeting with Franklin & Marshall.

Saturday, F&M will play C [illegible] in at noon, and the tw [illegible] leyans will hook up at 2.

articles.headline: Women's Volleyball
articles.author: By REBECCA SHOUP Staff Reporter
articles.body:
The women's volleyball team expects to do better than last year.

"Generally we want to play more consistently," said Coach Mary Parker.

Returning seniors Rebecca Roush, Amy Decant, and Amy Wood will lead the new Bishop squad.

"The freshmen look good," said captain Amy Wood. "We expect to win at least half of our games."

Before the open tryout was held on Monday, the three new freshmen on the team were Elizabeth Stuller, Penny Sorrell and Andrea Starr. All three women played volleyball in high school and were recognized as valuable players.

The team's toughest game will be Oct. 14 against Alleghany.

"We gave them (Alleghany) competition last year, so I think we'll be able to give it to them again this year," Wood said.

articles.headline: Young teams plague cross country
articles.author: By TOM HALSTED Staff Reporter
articles.body:
Youth and lack of college experience are the two main problems facing both the men's and women's cross country teams entering the 1988 season.

The men's team, which finished 3-8 in dual meets and last at the North Coast Athletic Conference championships, returns three runners from last season: junior Malcolm Doyle and sophomores Mike Colson and Tom Trafton. The team is relying on freshmen additions to boost its record.

"Our success will be based on how our six freshman come through and contribute," said coach Marv Frye.

Competition in the NCAC will be a strong, led by Wooster and Case Western Reserve.

"We have a very tough conference," Doyle said. "A lot of the schools have many returning lettermen. With a young team, it will be hard for us to move up in the conference."

The men's team is young; the women's team is younger. Sophomore Cathy Sell is the only Bishop with previous collegiate experience, and no one is back from the team that finished fifth at the NCAC Championships last year.

"We have fifteen very solid runners; eleven of them are freshmen," coach Alison Stanford admitted. "It's tough to tell who will be the strongest runners."

Back from last spring's outdoor track season are Sell, junior Kathy Rogers and sophomores Renee Dadik and Marcia Benzaquen. Freshman possibilities include Tara Craig, Diane DelBalso, Ann Kreitz, Dawn Mullineaux and Jennifer Schultz.

"We're hoping for a top-three finish (in the NCAC) to make it to regionals," added Stanford.

Doyle summed up the outlook for both teams.

"We're very excited with the number of freshmen coming," he said. "I think with some hard work we can have a productive season."

articles.headline: Linksters expected to place near top in preseason poll
articles.author: By ANDY CRAWFORD Staff Reporter
articles.body:
When the Division III preseason golf poll is released in the coming weeks, the Bishops are expected to make an appearance near the top of the list.

Acquiring any added pressure by a high national ranking does not surprise or concern head coach Dick Gordin.

"That's where we should be," said Gordin. "We had a strong finish last season and we're looking to do even better this time around."

Gordin has reason to be optimistic. The Bishops return the entire lineup that propelled them to the North Coast Athletic Conference championship and to a fourth-place finish at the national championships last sprin.

Senior Dan Wyant leads the attack. Wyant shot a 227 at last year's national tournament to earn second-team All-America honors.

Joining Wyant are juniors Todd Benware and Greg Wilhelm. Both are honorable mention All-America honorees, and Benware returns as the defending NCAC champion.

Wilhelm and sophomore Barry Pry were also named to the 1988 All-NCAC first team.

"I think we're going to have a really strong team," said Pry. "We are expecting a lot of positive things. We have a lot of freshman this year with quite a bit of experience, and our returning upperclassmen will help carry the team."

Competing for the fifth slot on the team are seniors Pat Maginnis, Jeff Harper and Steve Sanderson and sophomore Kevin Fillman. Newcomers to the squad include freshmen John Whithaus, Doug Borck and David Lit.

"We're going to have a very good season," said Gordin. "We've returned all the ingredients. Now it's just a matter of going to these tournaments and performing well."

The team plays a fall schedule of three tournaments and returns in the spring for its championship season.

articles.headline: Field hockey faces Hiram
articles.author: By NATALIE HURST Staff Reporter
articles.body:
The women's field hockey team will return from a 16-4-1 season last year to play Hiram next week.

Head Coach Nan Carney-Debord is enthusiastic about the upcoming season. A core of the returning players are also the strongest players, such as senior Robin Buckingham.

Carney-Debord said that the team will be successful if they play hard "game by game".

Denison and Wooster will prove difficult opponents later in the season from their extensive recruiting, she said.

articles.headline: Women’s soccer team kicks off season
articles.author: By TOM HALSTED Staff Reporter
articles.body:
Women’s soccer coach Margie Shade has a very simple goal for the 1988 campaign, which begins versus Mt. Union on Tuesday.

"Our main goal, besides winning the conference, is to win more games than we tie," Shade said.

Shade was referring to 1987, a frustrating year in which the Bishops went 1-1-4 in the North Coast Athletic Conference and 6-3-6 overall. The team showed promise, but was hurt by inexperience and injuries, including the midseason knee injury to Academic All-America Rachael Grant, now an assistant coach.

The Bishops are still young, but 13 letterwomen return from 1987, when 10 of 15 games were decided by a goal or less. That will help make the players mature sooner, Shade says.

Shade is very optimistic about her team. "Overall, our ball-(control) skills and mental attitude are the best I've seen."

Leading the way is junior goalie Molly Hewes, a Region 3 All-America and the NCAC Defensive Player of the Year last season. Over the summer, Hewes attended an advanced goaltender camp to improve on her 1.0 goals against average of last season.

"Our main goal, besides winning the conference, is to win more games than we tie."

Hewes is supported by three starting fullbacks. Junior Hilary Dove returns as the stopper, and sophomore Lisa Goodburn will probably move from left fullback to the sweeper position.

Midfield is anchored by senior co-captain Nina DeSimone and sophomores Leigh Sears and Betsy Theve. Their job will include distributing the ball to the wings, aggressively attacking the ball on defense, especially after the offense loses the ball, and scoring an occasional goal from the perimeter.

Last year's two top goal scorers, sophomores Mindy Parrish and Becky Furth, also return. Parrish scored 11 goals and 3 assists last year. Furth had 10 goals and 7 assists. Late in the season, however, they were very tightly marked by opposing defenses, and the team had trouble scoring.

"We'd like to have more versatility and more goal-scorers this year. We have better depth on the frontline. We'll have less pressure on Mindy and Becky," Shade said.

Shade's optimism is fueled by the result of Saturday's scrimmage against Otterbein, in which five different Bishops scored. Sophomores Elizabeth Hanna and Clarissa Holden were two of many players who showed strong improvement, Shade said.

"We showed better depth and versatility (in the scrimmage)," Shade repeated. "If we stay healthy, we should have a very good season."

articles.headline: Performing Arts Lecture Series
articles.author: By null
articles.body:
The Performing Arts Lecture Series as announced its schedule for the fall.

The series will begin with a performance by the Second City Touring Company.

Second City is a comedy troupe that has previously included Dan Aykroyd, Shelly Long, John Belushi, Bill Murray and many others. The group will appear Sept. 2.

On Oct. 21, The Publick Theatre Company will present its production of 'Much Ado About Nothing.

French pianist Jean-Yves Thibaudet will continue the series with a concert Nov. 1.

A two-man show called The Mask Men will appear Nov. 30.

Second City, Thibaudet and 'The Mask Men' will be presented in Gray Chapel.

'Much Ado About Nothing' will be performed in Chappelear Drama Center. Ticket information is available at extension 858.

articles.headline: Headroom to host video dance
articles.author: By KRIS ADAMO Arts and Features
articles.body:
Computer personality Max Headroom will host a dance party to benefit Special Olympics, Friday, Sept. 9.

The video concert will feature "a huge video screen" says Jeff Zeigler, director of campus programs. The stage will be set up over the floor of Branch Rickey arena. A fog and light show will also be featured.

The show will be sponsored by Club Coca-Cola.

"Club Coca-Cola sponsors concerts across the nation for the Special Olympics," Zeigler said. He added that there is a $2,400 charge for every university that hosts the party. Campus Programs, Marriott Food Service, and the MUB Pub divided the cost.

"Both Ohio University and Bowling Green have held this event in the past and there has been a tremendous turnout, a very strong response," Zeigler

said.

The dance party is an "A" event, meaning that no other social events will be held on campus that night.

The party will begin at 9 p.m. and last until 1 a.m. Admission will be free.

articles.headline: Film series set for Fall
articles.author: By null
articles.body:
The University Film Series will begin this weekend with screenings of "Planes, Trains, and Automobiles" a John Hughes film starring John Candy and Steve Martin.

The series continues with "The Seventh Sign," Sept. 16 -18 and "Pink Floyd -- The Wall" on Sept. 23-25. Michael Douglas' Oscar-winning performance in "Wall Street" will be shown Oct. 6-9. October also features "Good Morning Vietnam," Oct. 21-23 and "Fatal Attraction," Oct. 28-30. "Broadcast News" will be shown Nov. 4-6. "Willow" will be presented on Nov. 11-13. December brings "A Fish Called Wanda," Dec. 2-4.

Videotapes are now available to rent from the audio-visual section of the library. Jeff Zeigler, director of campus programs, says that 20 new video cassettes have been added to the collection. New titles include "Baby Boom", "Raising Arizona", and "The Big Chill".

The Ohio Wesleyan intramural sports department has released a full schedule for the fall semester.

The team sports and their starting dates are as follows:

Individual events for the fall semester include a racquetball tournament beginning Sept. 26; a 5K Turkey Run on Nov. 13; a wrestling tournament, Dec. 7 and 8; and a swim meet, Dec. 11.

In addition, an aerobics class has been set up at a cost of $25 for a 10-week session. There will be two free classes on Sept. 6 and 8 at 6:30 in Edwards Gym.

More information is available from Bruce Tall, director of intramurals, at ext. 500.
